data.title: Precious Metals Jump on Easing AI Jitters — Market Talk
data.description: Precious metal prices jump as investors return to the AI trade and global stocks rebound, boosting risk appetite across markets. Gold futures rise 3.8% to $3,671.90 a troy ounce, while silver soars 10.1% to $44.11 an ounce. Platinum is up 8.5% to $1,348.50 an ounce. "Beyond the technical nature of the rebound, the recovery also highlights the role of precious metals as an ATM in times of market stress," analysts at Saxo Bank say. "With AI-related technology stocks rebounding and broader risk appetite improving, the queue at the cash machine appears to be thinning, easing the liquidity-driven selling pressure." Still, the broader macroeconomic picture remains challenging, with traders expecting the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates at its next meeting in December and potentially next year as well. data.title: Indonesian nickel boss possibly involved in treason against Prabowo's government, official says
data.description:
Indonesian nickel businessman Arif Kurniawan was possibly involved in treason against President Prabowo Subianto's government, the head of the government's communications office was quoted by state news agency Antara as saying on Friday.

The comment about former Glencore trader Arif, named this week as a criminal suspect in alleged money laundering from 2021 to 2026 stemming from corrupt practices when obtaining a mining permit, follows an ongoing investigation launched after a former police chief was accused of wiretapping Prabowo.

Communications head Syahganda Nainggolan said Arif served as an "intellectual actor" in the operation, indicating that he was involved in orchestrating it. He added that Arif might already have fled to China, Antara reported.

"We see indications that a mining magnate, whose name is Arif Kurniawan, is among the intellectual actors because those intellectual actors are invariably backed by politics and oligarchic interests," he said.

Syahganda did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Friday. Reuters was unable to identify Arif's legal representatives and attempts to reach him by phone were unsuccessful.

According to the prosecutors, a mining businessman with the initials AK, identified by local media as Arif, controlled at least six nickel mining companies in Southeast Sulawesi, with licenses covering more than 4,000 hectares of mining concessions.

Local media have referred to Arif as a "nickel king".

The ongoing treason investigation was triggered by the arrest and dismissal of Indonesia's former police chief, Listyo Sigit Prabowo. He was charged with treason this week.

Listyo, who is not related to the president, allegedly ordered the unauthorised wiretapping of several figures, including Prabowo, police said.

The ousted police chief was widely regarded as being close to Prabowo's predecessor Joko Widodo, and the treason allegations have fueled speculation that ties between Prabowo and Widodo have become strained.

Treason charges are rare in Indonesia and carry a maximum penalty of death, Indonesian law stipulates.

data.title: International Gemological shares rise 7% as promoter proposes to sell 1.55% stake
data.description:
Shares of International Gemological Institute (IGI) rallied nearly 7 percent in intraday trade on Friday, November 27, after a large block deal, involving 67.16 lakh shares worth Rs 280 crore, took place on the bourses in the pre-open block window.

Around 67.16 lakh shares of International Gemological Institute, worth approximately Rs 280 crore, changed hands at Rs 417 per share in the block deal window. The company's promoter, BCP Asia II Topco Pte Ltd, is the likely seller in the transaction.

The number of shares that changed hands amount to 1.55 percent of the total outstanding equity of the company, in-line with what was disclosed earlier, reported CNBC-TV18.

In a regulatory filing dated November 26, IGI announced that its promoter, BCP Asia II Topco Pte. Ltd., an affiliate of US asset manager Blackstone Inc., intends to sell 67,16,031 equity shares, equivalent to around 1.55 percent of the company's total paid-up equity share capital, to comply with minimum public shareholding requirements.

The promoter has proposed the stake sale in multiple tranches before December 2, subject to the validity of the pre-clearance and applicable regulatory requirements, to comply with minimum public shareholding norms.

Currently, BCP Asia II Topco owns 33,08,35,803 shares in IGI, representing 76.55 percent of the company’s total paid-up equity share capital of 43,21,59,696 shares. After the completion of the proposed stake sale, the promoter's holding in the company is expected to decline to below 75 percent.

The promoter has also confirm that neither it nor any other member of the promoter group will buy IGI equity shares in the open market on the days the proposed sale is carried out.

IGI share price today

International Gemological Institute shares opened at Rs 430 and rallied as much as 6.6 percent to hit an intra-day high of Rs 451.25, compared with the previous closing price of Rs 423.20. With the gains, the stock touched its highest level in over a week.

However, the stock pared most of its intraday gains and was trading at Rs 428.20 apiece, up 1.18 percent, at around 1.35 pm.

Trading volumes also surged following the block deal announcement. Nearly two million shares of the company had changed hands on the exchange, which is over 12 times the volume traded until the same time Thursday and nearly 27 percent higher than the three-month average daily traded volume.

IGI share price history

IGI shares have gained nearly 1.5 percent in a week while it has surged over 10 percent in a month. The stock has also risen 28.59% on a year-to-date basis.

data.title: French Inflation Slides on Drop in Fuel Prices — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Ed Frankl

Inflation in France fell more than expected in November as fuel prices declined, but remained too high for the European Central Bank, which next month is expected to raise its key interest rate for a third time since the start of the war between the U.S. and Iran.

Consumer prices in the eurozone's second-largest economy were 3.2% higher than in the same month of 2025, a lower annual rate of inflation than the 3.7% recorded in October, France's statistics office said Friday. Economists polled last week by The Wall Street Journal expected a 3.6% rate of inflation.

Inflation in France climbed to its highest level in nearly three years in October, from an annual rate of just 1.1% in February, before the first U.S. airstrikes on Iran.

Oil prices have fallen since the outcome of U.S. midterm elections fueled hopes of a lasting resolution to the conflict, although they remain above prewar levels. As a result, prices of gasoline and other fuels have declined.

However, European natural gas prices remain near multiyear highs, which will keep household energy prices elevated throughout the colder winter months.

The ECB has raised its key rate twice so far this year, judging that the surge in energy prices was too great to ignore. Investors are primed for another hike before the end of the year.

The EU said last week that it expects French inflation to peak at 4.3% in the first quarter of 2027 due to further increases in energy prices and how they pass through into food and services.

Yet incoming data shows few signs of those energy costs spilling over into other parts of the economy. Services inflation, for instance, fell in November due to a sharp decrease in prices for accommodation and transport services.

It comes as France's economy appears to have been hit harder by the war than its neighbors. Gross domestic product sank 0.2% in the third quarter, dented by a drop in exports and lower private investment.

Investors have grown more concerned in recent months over the country's public finances, which sent government bond yields rising. Those higher bond yields, while ratcheting up nervousness around the economy, could help the ECB as they tighten monetary conditions before the central bank needs to raise rates.

French consumer spending was flat on month in October, data also published Friday showed, coming in the month when consumer confidence hit its lowest level in more than three years. While surveys of purchasing managers showed steady economic growth in Germany, there was a deepening downturn in activity in France.

In neighboring Spain, inflation also declined notably in November, falling to 4.1% from 4.9% in October, data published Friday showed.

Write to Ed Frankl at edward.frankl@wsj.com

data.title: Two Indian state-run financiers eye debut dollar debt before RBI window shuts, bankers say
data.description:
By Dharamraj Dhutia

State-run financiers India Infrastructure Finance Company (IIFCL.UL) (IIFCL) and UCO Bank plan to issue debut dollar-denominated bonds next month before the central bank's subsidised swap window closes, two merchant bankers said on Friday.

The plans come as US Treasury yields slide amid an unravelling of the global AI trade and investors flocking towards safe-haven assets, making the window, which closes on December 31, more attractive.

IIFCL could raise around $500 million through a five-year debt issue, while UCO Bank could add to the $1 billion fundraising it has already approved with a smaller size of around $250 million-$300 million maturing in three or five years, the bankers said.

The bankers requested anonymity as the matters are still private, while IIFCL and UCO Bank did not reply to Reuters emails for comments.

Some Indian firms had earlier pushed back their plans after a spike in Treasury yields made borrowing more expensive, the bankers said.

IIFCL recently held meetings with investors as part of a non-deal road show and received a BBB long-term rating from S&P earlier this month.

The debt of UCO Bank is rated BBB by S&P and BBB- by Fitch Ratings.

In June, the Reserve Bank of India announced measures to stabilise the rupee, including a subsidised hedging facility for lenders and state-run firms to lower their overall borrowing costs.

Indian lenders have so far raised $13 billion under the scheme.

In September, National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development raised dollar debt worth $750 million through 10-year papers at 6.1220%, or at a spread of 105 basis points above comparable US yields.

Power Finance Corp also raised $300 million through three-year bonds at a spread of 110 bps over US Treasuries.

data.title: Zcash Developers Race to Secure Crypto. Can Quantum Computing Break Bitcoin?
data.description:
Key takeaways

  • Zcash development team Zakura (November 26) called for accelerated retirement of the older Sapling privacy pool, which it estimated held about 400,000 ZEC.
  • A November 27 dashboard snapshot showed about 306,684 ZEC still in Sapling, though that does not prove the warning prompted anyone to move funds.
  • Zakura’s concern is speculative, unverified mathematical advances, not a successful quantum attack, and Shielded Labs expects to pick a post-quantum direction by the end of January 2027.
  • The Quantum Ledger counts about 7.23 million BTC (35.9% of issued supply) with public keys already visible on-chain; Glassnode’s May estimate was 6.04 million BTC.
  • No reliable date exists for a quantum computer that can break crypto signatures, but upgrading blockchains, wallets and custody could itself take years.

Can quantum computing break crypto? For years, the question has largely been treated as a problem for the distant future. Zcash developers, however, are already discussing what to do with hundreds of thousands of coins that could become vulnerable if certain cryptographic protections fail.

On November 26, Zcash development team Zakura called for the accelerated retirement of Sapling, an older privacy system that the team estimated still held around 400,000 ZEC. The recommendation followed speculation about mathematical breakthroughs at artificial intelligence laboratories.

A day earlier, Shielded Labs published its first technical update on a separate project designed to protect Zcash against future quantum computers.

Neither development means cryptocurrency has been cracked. Together, however, they raise a more pressing question: can blockchain developers replace the mathematics protecting investors’ money before someone finds a way around it?

What Is Quantum Computing?

Quantum computing is a way of processing information using the properties of quantum mechanics. Unlike conventional computers, which represent information using bits with a value of either zero or one, quantum computers operate using quantum bits, commonly known as qubits.

By manipulating these qubits, researchers can design algorithms capable of solving certain mathematical problems far more efficiently than conventional computers.

The important word here is certain. A quantum computer is not simply a faster version of the laptop sitting on your desk. Its advantages depend on the type of problem it is trying to solve.

Unfortunately for the cryptocurrency industry, some of those problems underpin the security of digital wallets.

As explained in NewsBTC’s guide to quantum computing, blockchains rely on cryptographic signatures to establish ownership and authorize transactions. A sufficiently powerful quantum computer could undermine some of the signature systems currently used to protect digital assets.

How Could Quantum Computers Steal Cryptocurrency?

When you send Bitcoin from your wallet, the network needs to establish that you have the authority to spend those coins. It does this by verifying a digital signature produced using your private key.

Your private key is supposed to remain secret. The corresponding public key can be disclosed because working backward from a public key to its private counterpart is computationally impractical using conventional methods.

Quantum computing could change that.

In 1994, mathematician Peter Shor introduced a quantum algorithm that could efficiently solve certain mathematical problems underlying modern public-key cryptography.

A sufficiently powerful quantum computer running such an algorithm could potentially recover private keys from exposed public keys. An attacker could then create a transaction that the blockchain would recognize as valid, even though the original owner had never authorized it.

That is a particularly uncomfortable problem for cryptocurrencies. Bitcoin does not have a customer service department that can reverse an unauthorized transfer.

The National Institute of Standards and Technology has already developed alternative cryptographic standards intended to withstand these future attacks. The challenge for crypto is incorporating such protection into networks that were originally built around different assumptions.

How Much Bitcoin Is Exposed to Quantum Computing?

Bitcoin’s public transaction history makes it possible to estimate how much of its supply could be exposed under certain quantum attack scenarios.

According to a November 25 snapshot from The Quantum Ledger, approximately 7.23 million BTC, representing 35.9% of issued supply under its methodology, was associated with public keys or spending scripts already visible on the blockchain.

Around 1.94 million BTC was classified as exposed because of its output design. A further 5.29 million BTC was associated with addresses that had previously revealed relevant spending information.

Some of these coins date back to Bitcoin’s earliest years, when transactions commonly revealed public keys directly.

Estimates vary between researchers because they do not all measure exposure in exactly the same way. In May 2026, Glassnode’s research identified 6.04 million BTC under its own classification framework.

These figures should not be interpreted as the amount of Bitcoin that will eventually be stolen. They measure a potential vulnerability under a specific future scenario, not an active attack.

Owners of many exposed coins could migrate their holdings if suitable protection becomes available. Dormant wallets whose owners have lost their private keys present a considerably harder problem.

Why Zcash Developers Want to Retire an Older Privacy System

Zcash offers a useful example of how complicated a cryptographic migration can become.

Unlike Bitcoin, where transactions are generally visible on a public ledger, Zcash provides privacy features through shielded pools. These allow users to transact without publicly revealing certain transaction details.

Sapling is one of the network’s older shielded systems. Its proof mechanism relies on mathematical assumptions that Zakura believes warrant additional scrutiny in light of potentially accelerating cryptographic research.

“

The time to prepare for a cryptographic breakthrough is before it happens.

Zakura · Sapling retirement proposal

Zakura proposed preventing new deposits into Sapling while encouraging users to migrate to Ironwood, a newer privacy system. If credible evidence of a threat emerged, further emergency measures could be considered.

The amount involved is already changing. A November 27 snapshot from the Zcash Dashboard, timestamped 06:06 UTC, showed approximately 306,684 ZEC remaining in Sapling, below the rounded estimate cited in Zakura’s proposal. The difference does not, by itself, establish that the warning prompted users to move their funds.

The discussion follows Zcash’s recent NU7 network upgrade, which improved transaction speed and continued the network’s transition away from older infrastructure.

Importantly, the immediate concern raised by Zakura is not evidence of a successful quantum attack. It relates to speculative advances in mathematics that could affect particular cryptographic constructions. Those advances remain unverified.

Can Zcash Become Quantum-Resistant?

On November 25, Shielded Labs published an update on its Epoch project, which aims to develop privacy technology capable of withstanding future quantum computers.

One of the problems its researchers are working on is the size of cryptographic proofs.

Stronger protection can require considerably more data to be processed and transmitted. That can create difficulties for blockchains, where transaction capacity, verification costs and storage requirements already matter.

The team is evaluating two possible approaches and expects to select a direction by the end of January 2027, provided its research progresses as planned.

Ironwood already incorporates features intended to support a future recovery mechanism. However, the developers have made clear that these features do not make Zcash fully quantum-resistant today.

The distinction is important. Having a contingency plan for a future attack is not the same as having protection against one.

Are Bitcoin and Ethereum Preparing for Quantum Computing?

Zcash is not the only network confronting these issues.

Bitcoin developers are discussing changes through proposals including BIP-360, which would introduce a transaction output format designed to reduce certain forms of public-key exposure.

A separate draft, BIP-361, explores a gradual transition away from vulnerable signature schemes once suitable alternatives are available.

Neither proposal should be confused with an activated Bitcoin upgrade.

Ethereum faces additional complications. Beyond individual wallets, its security model relies on cryptographic signatures used by validators and other infrastructure.

Ethereum’s quantum-security challenge extends to staking arrangements and institutional custody.

There is also a governance problem that applies particularly to Bitcoin. If millions of coins remain in old wallets that cannot be migrated, should the network eventually restrict their movement to prevent potential theft?

Doing so could protect the broader ecosystem, but it could also prevent legitimate owners from accessing their own money. Leaving those coins untouched carries a different set of risks.

Cryptography alone cannot settle that argument.

When Will Quantum Computing Become a Real Threat to Crypto?

There is no reliable date for when a quantum computer capable of breaking widely used cryptocurrency signatures will become available.

Building such a machine requires more than increasing the number of qubits. Those qubits must also be reliable enough to carry out lengthy, complex calculations without errors overwhelming the results.

According to Coinbase Institute’s research, the relevant machines do not yet exist, but the process of upgrading blockchains, wallets and custody infrastructure could itself take years.

For that reason, waiting for an actual attack before implementing stronger cryptography would be a risky approach.

Crypto investors should pay attention to what developers implement, whether wallets support the new protections and whether existing funds can be migrated without compromising ownership.

There is no need to buy a token simply because its developers describe it as quantum-resistant, either. Such claims deserve scrutiny of the underlying cryptography and its implementation.

Zcash’s latest proposals offer a glimpse of the decisions other blockchain communities may eventually face. Replacing an algorithm is one thing. Persuading an entire decentralized financial network to move its money before a deadline is something else entirely.

data.title: European Insurers Might Face Difficult Year Ahead — Market Talk
data.description: European insurers are likely to face challenges in 2027, with relative valuations at all-time highs, J.P. Morgan analysts write. The sector outperformed in 2026 despite JPM's cautious view, the analysts note, with a strong rerating in valuations in the second half of the year. As a result, valuations are now high, but earnings revisions are lagging, and there is a poor property & casualty pricing environment in the commercial sector and reinsurance, the analysts note. JPM says it is difficult to be positive about insurers heading into 2027, and maintains its cautious stance. JPM prefers life insurance stocks, which might benefit from structural growth drivers. (michael.hennessey@wsj.com)
